calibration.reason: The repair intake is legible and clearly labeled, but its familiar layout is not especially distinctive and misplaced focus after invalid input impairs recovery.

primary_action.input: Tab, then Right Arrow from the selected 4 m radio
primary_action.expected: Select 6 m and show the path, ferry and footbridge closures.
primary_action.observed: 6 m was selected with visible focus; the list showed all three closures.

A-1440.edge_observation: Right Arrow wrapped to 2 m; the list contained only Riverside path closes.
A-1440.fact_check: The captured 6 m water line aligns with the 6 m mark and the text. The closure thresholds match the task; their real-world accuracy was not independently verified.
A-1440.strength: The large cross-section connects each threshold to a clear, compact closure list.
A-1440.weakness: The illustration labels are visually prominent enough to compete with the selected level and results.
A-1440.repair: Give the selected level and closure heading slightly stronger priority while retaining the diagram labels.

primary_action.input: Tab, then Right Arrow from the selected 4 m radio
primary_action.expected: Select 6 m and show all three closures.
primary_action.observed: 6 m was selected with visible focus and all three closures appeared.

A-390.edge_observation: Right Arrow wrapped to 2 m; the list contained only Riverside path closes.
A-390.fact_check: In the immediate after capture, the text reads 6 m while the visible water line is below the 6 m mark. A transition may explain this, but the settled 6 m image was not captured; agreement cannot be confirmed from this evidence.
A-390.strength: The diagram, controls and results fit together in a readable single-column view.
A-390.weakness: The diagram's labels and scale become small on mobile.
A-390.repair: Increase mobile diagram label legibility and ensure the displayed water height settles consistently with the selected value.

primary_action.input: Tab through the slider and closure buttons to Footbridge, then Enter
primary_action.expected: Jump to 6 m and show the path, ferry and footbridge as closed or stopped.
primary_action.observed: The value became 6 m and all three rows showed closed or stopped, with focus on Footbridge.

B-1440.edge_observation: Two Shift+Tabs and Enter selected 2 m. Only the path was marked closed, but all three rows remained in the list; ferry and footbridge said Level not reached.
B-1440.fact_check: The immediate 6 m capture shows the water line above 4 m but below the 6 m mark, despite the 6 m text. A transition may explain this; a settled 6 m image was not captured. Real-world closure thresholds were not independently verified.
B-1440.strength: The status count and explicit labels distinguish reached from unreached thresholds.
B-1440.weakness: The closure rows function as jump controls, but their interactive purpose is not evident from their appearance; the 2 m list also retains unreached rows.
B-1440.repair: Make jump controls visibly recognizable and separate unreached crossings from the current closures list.

primary_action.input: Tab through the slider and closure buttons to Footbridge, then Enter
primary_action.expected: Jump to 6 m and show all three closures.
primary_action.observed: The value became 6 m, all three rows showed closed or stopped, and the Footbridge row had visible focus.

B-390.edge_observation: Two Shift+Tabs and Enter selected 2 m. The path alone was marked closed; ferry and footbridge remained listed as Level not reached.
B-390.fact_check: The immediate 6 m capture shows the water line below the 6 m mark while the value reads 6 m. A transition may explain this, but the settled image was not captured.
B-390.strength: The full set of controls and status rows remains visible in the mobile viewport.
B-390.weakness: Small diagram labels and visually understated row controls make the diagram and direct-jump affordance harder to read.
B-390.repair: Enlarge diagram labels and expose the row buttons as level-selection controls.

preference.reason: A makes the requested keyboard jump quickly and its 2 m list contains only the active path closure. Its desktop 6 m capture also aligns the water line with the labeled level. B provides useful unreached statuses, but retains those rows in the closures list and its immediate 6 m capture does not establish visual agreement with the text.

decision: The candidate wins the initial comparison. Continue refining mobile label legibility and emphasize the selected elevation. Keep the direction experimental below 9.5.
